forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter

news_drafts.headline: Northumberland County Council lists continued review of Advance Northumberland refinancing options
news_drafts.lead:
Northumberland County Council will continue its strategic review of refinancing options for Advance Northumberland, according to the annual report of its Cabinet Member for Finance and Value for Money, prepared for the County Council meeting on 4 November 2026.

The report lists the review among its forward actions, in the words "Continue the strategic review of refinancing options for Advance". It describes the review as aiming to settle the company's future operating and governance model.

The report gives no outcome from the review so far, no amount and no date for a decision.
news_drafts.paper_title: Cabinet Member for Finance and Value for Money Annual Report

news_drafts.headline: Northumberland accounts cleared as external audit finds no weaknesses
news_drafts.lead: Northumberland Council's 2024/25 accounts have received an unqualified audit opinion — meaning the external auditor Forvis Mazars found no significant weaknesses and fully approved the financial statements. The Audit and Standards Committee, meeting on 23 September, noted the clean bill of health from the independent audit. The Committee raised questions, however, about internal audit coverage and whether it adequately supported the council's 'Reasonable' opinion on governance and control arrangements. The Committee also noted that Adult Social Care and Children's Services received a high proportion of 'Outstanding' or 'Good' inspection ratings during the year.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Annual Report from Audit and Standards Committee to Council

news_drafts.headline: Northumberland borrows more despite cutting capital spending as reserves drain
news_drafts.lead: Northumberland County Council increased its external borrowing by £64 million in the year to March 2026 while reducing its cash reserves by £17 million and holding back £134 million of planned capital spending. External debt rose from £831 million to £895 million even though the underlying financing requirement — the amount the council actually needed to borrow for long-term assets — increased by only £43 million. The council's schools funding deficit more than doubled to £20 million, and it drew down other reserves to cover day-to-day costs. Capital spending ran 11 per cent below budget, with the council deferring projects. The mismatch signals the council is relying on borrowed money to fund running costs rather than investment in long-lived assets.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 Council Tax Support Scheme 2027 Cabinet 27-10-26
findings.headline: Cross-party group concluded the January 2026 exemption for households with a disabled adult or unpaid carer is not feasible at present
findings.detail: The January 2026 budget amendment made approval conditional on exempting these households from reductions in maximum support, and asked for a report within 6-12 months. The working group concluded that the practical implications and financial impact meant the exemption was not feasible at the present time.
findings.matters: A council declining to implement a condition attached to its own approval of a scheme is a governance decision that other councils and the council's auditors would look at.
findings.quote: was not feasible to introduce this at the present time

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 Council Tax Support Scheme 2027 Cabinet 27-10-26
findings.headline: Eligible households rose from 14,877 at the end of March 2026 to 14,967 at 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The paper attributes changes in eligibility mainly to household income changes, the migration of residents from legacy benefits to Universal Credit, and the removal of the two-child limit from 6 April 2026. The proposed scheme is modelled on a caseload of 14,699 claimants.
findings.matters: Growth in the number of households eligible for support drives the cost of the scheme and the council tax base, and the paper ties this growth to national benefit changes.
findings.figures: 14,877 eligible households at end March 2026; 14,967 eligible households at 30 September 2026; 14,699 claimants in the modelled caseload
findings.quote: at the end of March 2026 there were 14,877 eligible households

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 Council Tax Support Scheme 2027 Cabinet 27-10-26
findings.headline: The one-off £1.000 million hardship fund has made 36 awards worth £16,429, as at 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: Of 647 claims processed, with 10 still under assessment, 36 awards were made. The paper says the fund was set as a one-off budget and is not recurrent. The working group wants unused 2026-27 amounts kept for future years, but the paper says future use is a wider budget decision.
findings.matters: Low take-up of a one-off hardship budget, and the open question of whether the unspent balance is kept or reallocated, is a reserve decision other councils make in the same way.
findings.figures: £1.000 million one-off budget; 647 claims processed; 36 awards; £16,429 awarded
findings.quote: 36 awards were made at a value of £16,429

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 Council Tax Support Scheme 2027 Cabinet 27-10-26
findings.headline: Northumberland reassessed 1,794 cases affected by the Carers' Allowance and Employment & Support Allowance anomaly, and 1,488 of them saw a change in council tax due.
findings.detail: The anomaly arose from different treatment of two DWP benefits depending on whether the recipient was paid through Universal Credit. Enforcement action for impacted households was paused while the cases were reassessed. The paper says all cases were reassessed by 30 June 2026.
findings.matters: A scheme design error that required reassessing and rebilling a large number of cases, with enforcement paused, is a control and administration issue other billing authorities could face.
findings.figures: 1,794 cases assessed; 1,488 cases with a change in council tax due
findings.quote: with new bills issued where the level of support changed compared to the initial council tax bill

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 Council Tax Support Scheme 2027 Cabinet 27-10-26
findings.headline: Cabinet proposes lowering support in bands 2 to 4 for 2027-28, after the working group accepted that additional budget growth was "not a viable option".
findings.detail: The working group agreed that the scheme had to fit the existing financial envelope, so some bands had to change. It proposes keeping band 1 at 100% and band 5 at 20%, and reducing bands 2, 3 and 4 by five percentage points each. The paper says the forecast cost of correcting the anomaly was the reason for the change.
findings.matters: Reducing support to hold cost within a fixed envelope shifts the cost to households and changes the council tax base that the council will rely on for 2027-28 and later years.
findings.figures: band 2 90% to 85%; band 3 70% to 65%; band 4 40% to 35%; band 1 100% and band 5 20% unchanged
findings.quote: It was accepted that additional growth in the budget available was not a viable option

daily_post.headline: Citizens Advice Northumberland argues that higher liabilities would increase non-payment, arrears and court summonses, and that this would offset the council's expected savings.
daily_post.lead: Reduced discounts can raise collection costs and bad debt as well as bills, so the net yield from the change depends on collection performance. Other councils considering similar cuts can test this argument against their own arrears data.
